utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before the Prosecution is invited and before we go into closed session to hear the testimony of Witness RM070, it is on special request that you first read the summary, Ms. Marcus. You have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. RM070 is a woman in her late 40s from Foca municipality. She will testify that in the first week of July of 1992, uniformed and heavily armed Serb soldiers detained more than 30 Muslim civilians in the woods, including women, children, and elderly, in a village in Foca municipality. She will testify that the Serb soldiers swore at the civilians using ethnic slurs, and that shortly thereafter, the Serb soldiers shot and killed first three, and later seven more, of these Muslim civilians. The accused has been charged with these killings in indictment Schedule A2.1. RM070 will testify that the Serb soldiers then lined up the detainees, separated the women from the men, and that the women and at least one man were taken to Buk Bijela, where they were interrogated and subjected to both sexual and non-sexual torture. The accused has been charged with crimes committed in the detention centre at Buk Bijela in indictment Schedule C6.3. RM070 will then testify that numerous women and girls who were among the detainees were then taken to the Foca high school, Srednja Skola, where they were detained by Serb soldiers yet again. The witness will describe the daily and relentless pattern of rape and other forms of sexual and non-sexual torture to which the women and girls were subjected by Serb soldiers during their detention in the high school. The accused has been charged with crimes committed in the Foca high school in indictment Schedule C6.5. RM070 will testify that the women and girls were then transferred to the Partizan sports hall where they were enslaved and subjected to a daily pattern of humiliation, verbal assaults and threats, and violent acts of sexual violence. The accused has been charged with crimes committed in the Partizan detention centre in indictment Schedule C6.4. RM070 will finally testify that the Serb soldiers transferred the Muslim women and girls from Partizan to a house near Miljevina known as Karaman's house. Here, the Serb soldiers continued to subject the detainees to enslavement, verbal abuse and threats, rape, including frequent gang-rapes and sexual slavery. The accused has been charged with crimes committed in Karaman's house in indictment Schedule C6.2. That concludes the public summary, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Marcus. The witness will testify with protective measures being face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym. Therefore in order to hear the testimony of the witness, we first have to move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness RM070, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Witness RM070.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness RM070, you'll first be examined by Ms. Marcus. I take it that you know her already. You find Ms. Marcus to your right. Ms. Marcus, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 30311 - this is the witness's pseudonym sheet - but not broadcast it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, when the document appears on the screen in front of you, I'd like you to -- I'm sorry, I'm just waiting for the document. Yes. Could you please confirm without saying your name that that is your name?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: I don't have that anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is that your name which appears on the page in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And can you confirm that that is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender 65 ter 30311 into evidence under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30311 receives number P2421, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, do you recall giving a statement to the ICTY on the 15th to the 18th of November of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I would ask that 65 ter 30309 be placed on the monitor but not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is this the statement that you see in front of you that you gave to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we turn to the bottom of this page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, would you please look at the signature on the bottom of this page. Do you recognise this as your signature?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity before testifying today to review a translation of this statement in your own language?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today as you were asked when you provided this statement, would you provide the same answers, in substance?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Well, yes, I think so. It was a long time ago. However, I believe that my answers would still be the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the accuracy and truthfulness of this statement?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I tender this document, 30309, into evidence, under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30309 receives number P2422, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. When I said admitted, the document was admitted, although I had not yet heard the number. Apologies for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, you testified previously in a case before --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is admitted under seal. When I said admitted, of course, I meant admitted under seal. But it is already the first time I said under seal. But let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, you have testified previously in a case before this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And have you had the opportunity to review a segment of that prior testimony in preparation for your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions you were asked when you provided that testimony, would you provide the same answers, in substance?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the accuracy and truthfulness of that testimony?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender the selection of pages from the witness's prior testimony into evidence, please. That is 30310, under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, you asked about one segment, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This was the segment that was in the 92 ter application. I'm trying to avoid giving page numbers or identifying the case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I see that. But the sequence is -- it seems to be two segments rather than one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. It's not a contiguous -- it's not one contiguous segment. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if that is clear to the witness and the witness has listened to it. You had a opportunity to listen to two portions of your previous testimony? Did you have a opportunity to listen to that previous testimony, audio, listening, or did you read it or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just perhaps the witness might be confused because since it was just a short segment we had a language assistant translate it to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is, for us, a bit uncommon. So I do understand that you sat together with someone who read it in your language and then you confirmed that this was your truthful testimony at the time; is that right --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, the number to be assigned to the excerpt of the transcript would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30310 receives number P2423, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please have private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session. Witness, we now move into private session which means that not only no one will see you, not only -- no one will hear your own voice but even whatever you say is not to be made public.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, you describe Buk Bijela in your statement in paragraph 27 as a construction site for a proposed hydro-electric power plant. Can you tell us, if you know, what was this facility to the armed forces who captured you at the time of your detention? What purpose did Buk Bijela have to the Serb soldiers at the time you were detained there?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: They used it to torture and rape Muslim women whom they had captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 38 that on your way from Buk Bijela to the Foca high school in the bus, the bus stopped in front of the SUP. Were there police or soldiers at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: There were both police officers and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you a few clarifications regarding the detention in Foca high school. You say in paragraph 41 that two policemen guarded the entrance to the school day and night. Did you come to understand whether there was a superior/subordinate relationship between the police guards and the Serb soldiers who came and took out women and girls each night for sexual violence?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: I didn't see that. But when the soldiers came to the secondary school to take out women, nobody dared oppose them. Once, police officer Dragan Zelenovic opposed the soldiers, but he -- the soldier punched him with his fist so hard that nobody else dared to oppose them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When the Serb soldiers took you and other women and girls out of the Foca high school in the evening to the Brena apartments, did they try to avoid anyone seeing them? Did they do this in a secretive manner?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You describe in paragraphs 59 to 62 that while you were detained in the Foca high school, some TV cameras came to film you and the other detainees. Did you come to know why they were filming you? Why did they come to that detention centre to film you?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Well, you know, it was like this: They put me up at the secondary school, and we got three meals a day, and we had those sponges on which we slept. And then a man came and told us that television would come and film to show how they were protecting us and how they had saved us. And then I asked myself, From whom have they saved me? How I was attacked so that I needed saving? And when Belgrade TV arrived and TV S from Pale I was sitting in a corner of the room. I never once took a look to see who had entered and came to record. How could I say that they had saved me and protected me when I was being raped by a dozen or two dozen of them every night? They were lying shamelessly. They killed my mother and my brother. They killed everything in me. And now I was supposed to say that Mitar Sipcic saved me. I thought he was a human being. That's what I thought. I had known him from before because he worked at the infirmary at Brod as medical staff. So I never saw who had come and who recorded. But I know what they wanted. Their objective was propaganda to show how they were humane, that they had saved us and that they were protecting us. From whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you like to take a little break?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: It's all right. We can go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a few questions now about Partizan. Can you tell the Court how far Partizan is from the centre of Foca town.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: It's not far. If we take the square as the centre of Foca, then it's no further than 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 11159C which is a photograph from Foca. For the Court Usher's information, I will be asking her to make a few marks on here, so maybe they could assist her.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, there are already some numbers on this photograph. Can you identify what each of these numbers represent, please. Let's start with number 1.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Number 1 is -- oh, sorry, I must have done something wrong ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You won't need to mark numbers 1, 2, 3, or 4. You may need to mark something after that.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Okay. Number 1 is the Partizan gym; number 2 is the SUP; 3, I can't really tell now. This may be the municipality building. Across the road from the SUP, there were also women locked up and I heard screams from there every night. A number of women were locked up there and raped. And number 4 is the Zelengora hotel. Next to that hotel there is another house where I was also detained by Serbian soldiers. It's across the road from the textile factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So at the location you said: "Next to that hotel there is another house where I was also detained by Serbian soldiers." Could you mark that with the number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: I can mark it, but I'm not certain that it will be the very house. I think that it's this house here, where the arrow is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Please mark it with a 5. Right on the screen. You can write on the screen.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Number 5 is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The marking doesn't work at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was there any other location on this photograph that you wanted to indicate for the Court? If not, we can just continue. It's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can describe it for the transcript. The witness pointed at a house which is found immediately below 4, but not large construction, but the one with the red roof immediately right to that large construction. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I tender this photo into evidence, please. That's 65 ter 11159C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I don't think it needs to be under seal, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 11159C receives number P2426, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Ms. Marcus, we're close to the moment where we usually take a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have perhaps about ten more minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll first take that break. RM070, we first go into closed session, then you can leave the courtroom. We take a break of approximately 20 minutes, and after the break, you'll be further examined by Ms. Marcus for another ten minutes approximately, and then you'll be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence. We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Marcus, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, you describe in your statement at paragraph 90 being detained at Karaman's house. In your evidence, you mention a 12-year-old girl named Almira Bektovic. Was she also sexually assaulted?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was she the youngest?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to her afterwards?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: No, I don't. She's missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In paragraph 102, you say: "That night Klamfa negotiated with Dragan Stankovic about the sale of Almira. I heard that Klamfa sold Almira to Stankovic for 200 Deutschemarks." Is this Almira Bektovic you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe the circumstances of this so-called sale of Almira ?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, I just have a few more questions for you. In paragraph 98 of your statement, you say that you were "forced to make the sign of the cross." Can you tell us about this incident, please, if possible in brief.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: That was in Miljevina after I had already spent three months in that house. That was on the 13th [as interpreted] of October, I believe, in 1992. Janko Janjic, Dragan Zelenovic, Gojko Jankovic and somebody else came to the Karaman house where Pero Elez kept us. Pero told me in the morning that four of us had to go to Foca. Milorad Cicmil also came. I believe that he was a teacher in a school somewhere, as far as I could hear from others. They lined us up. There were eight of us girls. They sat us done and then he asked our names. Obviously we gave him Serbian names. And then he asked us whether we had learned how to make the sign of the cross. Since I was the first sitting down in that line, I didn't know the difference between the three fingers and the whole hand. I started making the sign of the cross with the whole hand. And all of a sudden he jumped up and he shouted at me, Do you want me to cut your hand off? You don't use your whole hand but only three fingers. And I said, I apologise, sir. I did not know. I did not attend the proper course, so I don't know. That's how they took the four of us and took us to Foca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, may I ask you for one clarification. You said it was on the certain day in October in 1992. Can you repeat the day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 30th of October, I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that from the 2nd of August, 1992, to the 30th of October, 1992, we were kept in that house. All in all, three month, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: One more clarification on your answer there. Who was it who instructed you about crossing yourself? Could you repeat the name, please.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: What did I say? Cicmil or Cicmal, Milorad.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's fine. RM070, this may be a difficult question to ask but it's nearly my last one. Did you ever come to learn whether there was any reason that you and the other women and girls were being so badly mistreated? What was the goal of this mistreatment, if any?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: My opinion was that they wanted to destroy, kill, destroy our spirit as much as they could, because a raped woman -- there's no cure for a woman who was raped. I will not recover. I cannot recover, ever. I'm trying. I'm trying very hard. My life was destroyed. My family was destroyed. The dearest to me were killed. All that I had in life, they took my happiness. I was a happy person. You -- one could not describe the level of my happiness. That's how I felt. But not all the Serbs are the same. Because if there were -- there hadn't been for some Serb, I wouldn't be sitting here today. Because there are some good people among the Serbs, but they couldn't do anything. They didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, is there anything else that you would like the Chamber to know, other than what you've told them in your statement or in your testimony so far?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: What -- what I have come here to say and what I have said so far, so many innocent victims. There are so many. And perhaps this is my way of finding comfort, finding solace. So far I've always felt as if I owed something to somebody because I'm alive. My brother is dead. My mother is dead. My uncle, my aunt, their children, they're all dead. And I'm alive. And so many people are dead. I've always felt dead towards them because I'm alive. I still feel that I owe them. This is the feeling that I have: That I owe them because I'm here. I have this feeling of guilt. I feel guilted. And that's why I had to come here to tell you the truth. Because all of all of those innocent victims who were killed. Because they were not guilty. They were innocent. My brother had just come back from the army in March, and four months later he was killed. He had returned from the Yugoslav army. We were proud of him. We were proud of the Yugoslav army. They brought cannons and tanks to Foca. The whole city was shaking with the sound of cannons and tanks, and we didn't know what they were up to. We didn't know why they were all coming our way. We didn't know what the purpose was. All that was predesigned. All that had been agreed in advance. It had been agreed in advance that Muslims had to be killed and destroyed. Our neighbours, Serbs, would be happy if we returned, if we lived with them, because these people say that once we left, everything's gone. They don't have anything. They're poor. I -- I feel sorry for them when I see how they live and how retched they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: RM070, thank you so much for answering all my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no more questions for the witness. I just wanted to ask the Chamber for leave to make one bar table submission at the -- at the end, when the witness has been excused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Stojanovic is aware of the bar table admission you intend --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Witness RM070, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We'll try to make it as short as possible. We will probably not use all the time that we asked for, and in view of the answers we have provided -- I supposed that you probably understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, good morning.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will have just a few questions for you. I don't want to remind you unnecessarily of those awful events, and I need to tell you that I'm sorry for everything that you had been through. But let's try and see if we can go through the document that we received earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to call up the document whose number I don't know but I believe that it has been marked for identification as a P document. And I'm talking about the list that the Prosecutor showed earlier this morning, the names of the people that the witness mentioned in her testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is P2424.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The document is under seal. It is P2424.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's just briefly go through the document, please, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We left it off at the moment when I asked you about the exchange. Please tell the Trial Chamber, according to what you remember, why is it that that exchange did not take place in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was really planned in the first place. I have my doubts about that. Again, it was propaganda. Nothing more. Both those soldiers in Cajnice as well as those in Foca were involved in the same propaganda because they did bring us there. They forced the villagers who were there to bring us food. They gave us cheese and cream. They forced us to eat a lot. We spent a night in a small school and then the next day they transferred us to a bigger school in Cajnice, all that allegedly awaiting for that exchange to take place. However, all that happened was that a TV crew came. I don't know from which TV channel. Again, they wanted to brag how kind and considerate they were, how helpful, and how they took care of us, and the TV crew recorded all that. But, again, I'm telling, I never spoke to any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In substance, did they tell you that the exchange did not go through because the opposing side in Gorazde did not accept the terms of exchange?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: They said that they did not want us and that there would be no exchange for that reason. Because our own people didn't want us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now I will finish with my last question: One of the Serb soldiers told you at one point in time that he would help you and that he would take you away from Foca. Please don't mention any names. Just confirm whether that is correct or not.

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. And I am grateful to him until the day I die.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Also, a neighbour of yours got involved in that journey, and he was the one who actually transferred you towards Bileca and Gacko and then on to Niksic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now into those two Serb soldiers you managed to get to what was then known as Titograd and today is known under the name Podgorica; right?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether after the war and after the implementation of property laws the villagers of your village got back their property?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there are Bosniaks still residing in your village who survived all those events that happened in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Only one man lives there. But he was never there before. He was not actually there during the war. He worked in Trebinje, in the military kitchen, and then he went to Montenegro, and there he spent the entire war. So he was not in the village during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not activated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I do not know whether it's Freudian that your microphone was not activated, but you announced the last question. We are a few questions further now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I meant the area, the last area, not last question. I have just one other sentence to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you tell me whether you still have contacts with the Serbs who helped you at the time?

utterances.speaker: RM070
utterances.text: Yes, with one. Not with the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam, once again. And on behalf of your -- of our client, I would like to apologise to you if I had caused you pain with any of my questions or if I have reminded you of those difficult and tragic events. And, once again, please accept my sympathy for everything that you had to go through. We apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, any need for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I have no questions. Just that I would like to tender into evidence P2424 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you've asked a few questions about the chart. Does the objection stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I had the opportunity to ask the necessary questions. We will continue to -- with our research into the names mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I say something about those names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not at this moment preferably. If there is any -- they are there, and the Defence has the possibility to verify the information you provided in the chart. Then P2424 is admitted into evidence, under seal. Witness RM070, the parties have no further questions for you. The Chamber has no further questions for you. If what you wanted to say about these names is your concern about having been mentioned, you can discuss that with the Victims and Witness Section after this hearing, and if there's anything of relevance, then the Victims and Witness Section will take the appropriate action. The Chamber would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. And the Chamber is fully aware what it takes to go to re-visit all these events you told us about and that even strengthens the thanks by this Tribunal that you have come forward and you have testified in this case. For you, in order to allow to you leave the courtroom with the protective measures, we first turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Marcus, while the furniture is removed, the -- you had one bar table document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to tendered 65 ter 2374A from the bar table in connection with the testimony of this witness. The Defence told me before court that they have no objection to this. What I would like to ask is that it be MFI'd for now. This is a small segment of one of the RS assembly sessions. And now, as Your Honours know, the Defence and the Prosecution are in the process of trying to agree upon which segments we would propose be admitted and Your Honours ultimately have to decide, so I would say that if this -- if more of this session comes in, it should all be under the same exhibit number. So I request a temporary exhibit number be -- be assigned to it. That's 2374A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's pending the possibility of joining with other parts of the same session. Madam Registrar, 65 ter 2374A receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P2427, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Is the Prosecution ready to continue -- oh, no. It's not the Prosecution. It's -- Mr. Hogan was being cross-examined. Therefore, is the Defence ready to continue its cross-examination of Mr. Hogan?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Hogan may be escorted into the courtroom. If you make a little bit more time, Mr. Usher, than usual, meanwhile, I read a decision. I'll deliver the following decision but we have to do it in private session, I see. So, therefore, could we briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The witness may be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I was just going to say that on Friday at transcript page 17611 Your Honour posed a question regarding P2380 which was the map with mount Trebevic on it about whether the elevations were included in those calculations. The witness was unable to answer but I can provide information to the Chamber, if the Chamber wishes, from the -- that I received from the mapping unit that could answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we first wait until we have finished. Just to complete the record, the Chamber has just been in private session to deliver its decision granting the Prosecution's 25th of January, 2013, motion to add three documents to its exhibit list. Mr. Hogan, welcome back in court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hogan. Here we go again.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We broke off while dealing with this document, and since it was last week I will ask for it to be displayed again, 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is 19792, and we need page 42 from this document. I have this page under a different number. Maybe we should -- give me one second. We'll try to locate the correct number of the page. I'll continue. But ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You remember the photograph with the rocky ground. It's related to the VP 6 incident. That is, from observation point number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have page number 52 because I'm -- I was informed that I was right. Yeah. Yeah, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember if the city of Sarajevo is on the left, as we're looking at this photograph?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It's towards the left of the camera, from the cameraman.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me when I say that if a mortar would to be placed here, it would be possible to target it from Muslim positions?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if a mortar was to be placed on that road where the camera was located, it would be possible to target it from Muslim positions. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes that is the question.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert, but it would just seem logical that if a weapon is firing in one direction and then another weapon could fire in the other direction, yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, Mr. Lukic, shouldn't we be seeing the road from which -- the one you are talking about, rather than this rocky incline?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it correct that we see a little part of the road on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. The bottom part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Bottom part of the left corner of the picture. Is that correct, Mr. Hogan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I establish that on my right screen looking e-court that especially -- exactly that part of the picture is missing in the left bottom corner, but we all apparently see that is visible a tiny little bit of what seems to be a road. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was actually if this position would, in such a case, be visible from the Muslim positions, the Muslim army positions.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, but I believe if we look at the -- either the photograph prior to this one or the photograph after this one, we should have a view to the left in the direction of the city. So we would be able to see what the view would be like.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot -- we cannot locate that picture. In a moment, maybe we might come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what page are we now at this moment, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we are at page 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fifty-two. I have a look nearby. Please proceed, meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You checked the road at this position. Did you find any traces of a mortar being dug in; and, if so, did you make a note of it?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any -- any signs of anything being dug in at this location, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see traces of digging in a mortar at some other location that you visited; and, if so, did you make a note of it?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any traces of anything being dug in at any locations, except for the normal farm work at the first location, the first two locations I stopped in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, would e-court page 47 of this document assist you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's the road where I was parked and -- and up to the right is that rocky slope. And I think he can see off in the distance to the left, would be part of the city, is visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me now ask you about firing position 10. You have already spoken about it. Do you remember -- let us take a look at the first page of this document. It's the page with the table which we saw briefly when the document was first displayed. Firing position 10 is marked as a position, the elevation of which is 1219 metres, and that would be the highest point of all that you -- that you visited. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get 65 ter 1D1297 from the Defence list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, in the centre of the photograph -- or, rather, in the centre horizontally but in the upper part, can you see a TV tower; and, if so, could you please circle it.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. WP 10, do you remember that the -- that point is to the right of this TV tower? It's actually the first promontory to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before we ask any further questions, what are we looking at at this moment? Which direction are we looking? Is that mount Trebevic at the end, is it another mountain?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is mountain Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least that's how you present it although we are not received any -- but you say this is a look at mount Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the -- the picture was taken from Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From Grdonj. That is more or less the direction south/north. No, no, I'm making a mistake. North/south. We all -- we have seen in evidence there are a few maps where Grdonj is indicated, and we know that where mount Trebevic is, so I think I made a mistake. It is from north to south, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you spot WP 10 in this photograph and is it the first summit to the right of the TV tower?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't spot way-point 10 in this photograph. Perhaps if I had that satellite image that we were looking at last week it might help me to orient myself to this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If it assists, I have the hard copies of the witness -- was in possession of last week of that and the index.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Lukic wants to use them, he certainly will appreciate your assistance, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's -- at least I have marked it as 65 ter 10441.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But, first, you should tender this, if you are interested in it, because you will lose the markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. Maybe I can ask another question before we leave this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, you told us on Friday that you know where OP-1 was; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark OP-1 on this picture.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to first orient myself with Colina Kapa, if you would just bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I would like to ask you to mark Colina Kapa as well, if you can.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would draw the outline of what I believe to be Colina Kapa. And I think OP-1 was in this area somewhere. It's a little bit difficult -- it's -- because this is not a three-dimensional photograph, it is a little bit difficult to be sure that that's exactly where Colina Kapa was but it's in the same -- general direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I agree with you where Colina Kapa is. Only, according to the marking I have, OP-1 was more to the left.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's my best estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties could try to agree later on on the basis of maps where OP-1 is situated and to see then whether they agree that this is the right or perhaps not an accurate marking by the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have this marked -- marked photo admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would appreciate if the witness could put OP-1 next to the second circle, to avoid any --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the bended line is the Colina Kapa. Madam Registrar -- well, I think it is only one banded line, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1297 as marked by the witness receives number D375, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were unable to locate way-point 10 in this photograph. But do you remember from your stay in the field that from way-point 10 there was a line of sight toward way-point 1; in other words, there were no obstacles between the two?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the distance from this point, OP-10, is some 2500 [as interpreted] metres from the Markale market, if we drew a straight line from it or if we look at the satellite image and we -- if we go by the straight line rather than follow the road?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I have two just points of clarification. One is when it says "OP-10" which is the -- where the witness said he was not able to locate, I don't know if Mr. Lukic meant way-point 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: WP 10. Yes, WP 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Way-point 10, we have the co-ordinates on the map, is there. They are given by the witness. And the second clarification you were seeking.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The other was when talking now about distances using this satellite image, I wonder if the Court would like the information about the elevation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because, Mr. Lukic, you know that we have two types of distances. The one is projected in a flat area as we find it on a map, and the other one, in which we include the inclination which makes the line longer than it looks on the map. Ms. Hochhauser, you have inquired into how the distance was measured in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes. I inquired with the mapping unit who actually made the map, and I was told that the elevations are not calculated in order to establish the distances between two points on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that the actual distance is longer than what is shown on the map on the scale available. Because the -- I always remember that it was called the hypotenuse is longer than the basis of a rectangular triangle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Common sense would agree with you but I -- I have not inquired any further than what I just relayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you asked about distance. What distance did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I see that it's wrongly -- maybe I misspoke but it says "2500." I wanted to ask more than 3500 and the distance I have is 3686 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But again what is the distance? Is that the projection of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that actually it would be more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It would be more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, can you tell us anything about whether the real distance which would be more than 3800, and forgive me, Mr. Lukic, but 76, or was it -- yeah, 86, whether that is it the -- whether that's the distance between that way-point and the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did not measure it. But I would not dispute it. If it had been measured it sounds reasonable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And Markale market, you're talking about Markale II, I take it, that covered not the open market but the covered market.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The covered marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I said 3800, of course I had to say 3600. I was misspeaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember that way-point 10 was a dominant point from which you could actually observe Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that way-point 10 was -- had a view towards the west so I don't think you could see the main part of the city but the very far western part towards Igman. I believe that we could see a view of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt again. But might I provide the witness with the satellite image so that he -- as he indicated it would be helpful --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- to him to answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted. Could the usher assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that way-point 10 does have a view to the east -- or, sorry, to the west. So I think we looked at some of those photos last week and compared them to one of the Defence photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see page 95 from the same document so maybe we can see more. 95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you want to refer to the number -- series of photographs, the approximately 100 with the table on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 65 ter, I think we have it on the screen, 65 ter 19792.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have on the screen at this moment a picture which was provided by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, that is right. My mistake, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the right document, I think. And then we -- you asked for page 95.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 95, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a picture from your collection. We can see a big part of Sarajevo. The photo was taken from that point; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This looks like it was taken from way-point 10 or way-point 6, looking towards the west. And I think that's Igman in the distance with Hadzici and Sokolica Colonija [phoen]. The airport is visible so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should I understand this as that the centre part of town is not visible here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now let me ask you something about way-point 5. Again from the table we can see that you say that that point is at a -- an altitude of 1073 metres. You were shown a photo from this document. The number is 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the page number 42 from this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember the place where you were? Has the photo jogged your memory?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in the direction that we are looking at, there is no elevation, there's no hill. The only obstacle is the forest. What I mean is that from the point where one is standing to take the photo and the city, there is no obstacle but the forest.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. The -- this photograph is from the view-point -- the camera is facing north towards the city and the ground falls away from the camera at this point but there are, as you point out, trees and forest, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that a shell fired from the mortar would be heard in the area behind this forest? In other words, that the forest would not be an obstacle to the sound. If you can agree with me; if not, we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this needs audiological expertise, isn't it? Unless you have established that the witness has it, apart from the fact that your question doesn't indicate at what distance, where, and, of course, a forest in itself does not stop sound, although it may have an effect. If you want the witness to answer this question, then please establish that is that good basis for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's look at the map that you have in front of you on the screen. It's 65 ter 10441. In this case, this is Exhibit P2380. If we project this on to the ground, this way-point is some 2800 metres from Markale; right? Would you agree with that estimate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which way-point exactly do you refer to, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Way-point number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 2800 metres, I would -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the azimuth is less than 180 degrees. Would you agree with that as well?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We did our calculations, and we came up with 167.4 degrees. Would you agree that this corresponds with the point that you marked as way-point 5?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not precisely measure it, but I'm not going to dispute that measurement that you made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you. [Interpretation] Way-point 4 is what you marked as being at 1080 metres. In the set of photos that you provided, together with way-point 4, we also find the photo depicted on page 33 of this document. However, we have to go back to 19792. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you have a few short questions, Mr. Lukic, that's okay. But, otherwise, we should take the break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take the break first. Could the usher escort the witness out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May we proceed?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to have page number 33 from the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a photo which you linked to way-point 4. Obviously it faces the city. You can actually see the city of Sarajevo -- Sarajevo from that point. Please remember this photo as we move on to the following page, page 34. This is Bistrik, the fortress of Bistrik. The previous photo, was it actually taken in the direction of Bistrik? Was that the way the camera was facing when the photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The previous photo that we saw before this one was oriented a bit further to the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And from where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, both this photograph and the previous photograph were taken from way-point 4 on the satellite image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me when I say that from way-point 4 there are no obstacles; i.e., there's no hilltop or any such thing between way-point 4 and the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From -- from the old city of Sarajevo, I would agree. Technically there is an obstacle if you're looking towards the western part of Sarajevo. There's a rise in the land further to the west of way-point 4. But for the old part of city -- of the city, I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you also agree with me when I say that there are no natural obstacles in the direction of observation point 1?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you just give me a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Observation point 1 is on the northern slope of Colina Kapa. So the actual crest of Colina Kapa would be between way-point 4 and observation point -- of post 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know the elevation of Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at this moment. I have seen the elevation on a map, but I -- I don't remember what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it lower or higher than way-point 4, which is 1080 metres?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it would be lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's focus on way-point 2, as well as on way-point 3. Would you agree with me if I said that these two points are both in Studenkovici village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever we are going back to the various way-points, could we have them on the screen. That is the -- I don't know ... that is the aerial photograph what the distance is and the lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P2380.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have it on our screens now. Could we zoom in on the way-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that way-point 3 and 2 are both in the territory of Studenkovici village?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that both these points, both way-point 2 and way-point 3, are located very high up on a very high elevation. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly is higher than the city of Sarajevo. I think it's about 1200 metres, if my memory serves me correctly, above sea level.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can I -- I'm sorry again to interrupt. But there is the index to these photographs that the witness doesn't have in front of him which marks the -- the relevant numbers, including the elevations so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you have index, can you provide it for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Rather than asking the witness to guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Lukic, you said are these and these way-points in Studenkovici. What is the relevance for us to know that it is in Studenkovici and not in any village by any other name?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It will be clear to us, Your Honour, when we will see, and we can see, if you want, we have [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say it will become clear then I'll patiently wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you also agree with me that this point is beyond the framework of 176 degrees, that it goes all the way up to 177 or even 178 degrees? I'm talking about way-point 3.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Way-point 3? Well, I think -- well, it may be a fraction of a degree off of 176 degrees. I tried to get on to the 176 degree line for both these way-points because they were the only two that I had access to along that azimuth. So it -- it may be a quarter of a degree to the west of the actual 176-degree mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you said it even goes to -- are you talking about the text or because if you look at it, it would be just -- it was touching upon -- is the middle of the curve which is, I would say, if you look at the whole of it, if you know that the two lines are 6 degrees apart, then it would be minimal, I would say. It's somewhere 176 and a half or something like that. But, of course, we would have to measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not an expert so I'm just following what my experts told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but -- experts. One of the first things you have to do with experts is first carefully consider whether they are right or wrong. And this is a matter of measurement. It has got nothing to do with -- to use a centimetre you don't have to be an expert. Unless the expert thought that the whole of the text WP 3 would cover the way-point, which is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It might be the case because only now we actually figured out through this witness that crescents are actually the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, so now you -- knowing this, you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Adapt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- adjust your questions to what you know now instead of relying on the experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] And now I'd like to call up 65 ter 1D1306 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now the people who work for us have looked at the map which they took from Google Earth, and they determined those points which, according to them, represent way-point 2 and way-point 3. And now the following photo. I -- I need 65 ter 1D1307. As a matter of fact, this depicts the village of Studenkovici and its general region. Would you agree with me that way-points 2 and 3 are the points that are hidden in -- on the sloping ground and not in the valley that is depicted in this photo?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- I believe the truck or lorry that's in the bottom right-hand corner is the same location where I parked to take the way-point GPS back in the summer of 2009. Sorry, 2007. So that -- I'm sorry, and that would designate way-point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, according to you, way-point 2 is the place where this lorry is parked.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where I marked the GPS where I stopped, and I took a way-point with my GPS and recorded those numbers, and that is what was marked as way-point 2 on my map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just bear with me for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is instructed not to speak aloud.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that case, I would abandon the investigation that was carried out by Colonel Demurenko, and since I have also abandoned the work produced by Mr. van der Weijden, I ask you in what way you participated in his work. And then we started discussing the incident known as F1. And now, in order for us to continue discussing the matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm still puzzled by what happens. I always understood that reading a GPS position was -- the outcome of that is more or less dictated by, first of all, the satellites and then, of course, by not misreading reading it. But, therefore, I'm a bit puzzled that both parties now have GPS readings which are the same but finding themselves in entirely different positions and, of course, I'm wondering what explains all this. Now, Mr. Hogan has told us, at least as far as I understand, and he has always photographed the GPS reading as well, as I saw in the hundred photographs, that still is a puzzle for me, but ... I -- I would invite the parties to see whether -- where it went wrong for whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless I'm misunderstanding, the prior -- the picture that was shown before this one, which was -- Mr. Lukic stated was their expert's explanation of where those way-points were, I don't think we've heard what that is based on and whether it's based on the same GS readings as Mr. Hogan received or the witness's understanding of the markings on that Mount Trebevic satellite. So I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is based on the markings and text rather than the crescent that might explain quite a bit. But, of course, GPS readings should be the same performed by either Prosecution or Defence. I'm just puzzled by it. Let's leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the only discrepancy is in regard of VP 4, in regard to the last one. Otherwise I don't see any other discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presently. We are looking now at way-point 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought we were looking at 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, my mistake, 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Apparently for way-point 2 then there is some disagreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now get D125 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since this document is an exhibit already and an identical photograph can be found in 65 ter 10270 on the OTP list, and the photograph was marked by Ms. Pita on the 25th of September, 2001. In this photograph, the house on the right -- actually, this roof is the incident site. It's here that the wounding took place.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this view-point is from the spot where the little girl had been standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us just remember this brick wall of the house facing the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's see 1D514.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a map of Sarajevo, and we circled three locations. I'll tell you what we consider them to be. Or, actually, I'll ask you. If you take -- or --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you look at the top circle, does it show the location of the house on Zagrecka Street where incident F1 took place?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The house is within that circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we look at the bottom circle, do we agree that it marks Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The circle in the middle encircles three symbols on a green surface. These symbols are crescents. Can you see them?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were at the site, do you remember visiting a Muslim cemetery; and could you locate it with respect to this centre circle?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've been past that cemetery many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D514 receives number D376, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Now, Mr. Lukic, if you want to depict an area, I can imagine you use a circle. If you want to depict a specific spot, I would not use a circle unless it is exactly that spot as in the centre of the circle, but then you'd do better by pointing at that centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe we can correct this map. Because I think the circles are proper for Baba Stijena, since it's larger area, and for cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe the witness could put the dot on this map where he thinks the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would ... I don't know what conclusions later will be drawn from it, but whatever the conclusions are, I take it that always the spot where the victim was hit plays a role.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's -- it's approximately there but it's on the -- and maybe if I could try this again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We can eradicate it and then do it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. Approximately there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then perhaps this document should be saved instead of the previous one. That will be our preferred solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, is it possible to replace the previous document by this one as the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the computer of the usher crashed, there'll be no possibility to save whatever. The previous one has been saved. Could we invite the witness to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Meanwhile you put some other questions to the witness and then we'll re-visit this issue, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I need usher's computer to see another photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions without photos, maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can proceed with different topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have to return to this question, sir. And I'll ask you about F12. Dzenana Sokolovic, age 31, and her 7-year-old son, Mervin, were fired on at Zmaja Od Bosne Street. Did you in the picture P136, did you see the UN GOFRS who were like firemen?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what the photograph -- which photograph you are referring to but I have seen a photograph and video with GOFRS in it at that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're probably speaking about the same thing. Once the system is up again, we can take a look. But did you see in that recording that the GOFRS, the members of that unit, were armed with pistols?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing the pistols, but I've seen other photographs not of -- of GOFRS but not at this sniping location where they have been armed, and I -- I have personal knowledge that they were armed. So that doesn't surprise me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you notice in the recordings, did you know otherwise, that they also had military weapons, such as sniping rifles?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the photographs of this sniping incident. I don't recall any such military weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I see that the three blue circles on the map are now available again. Perhaps you could ask the witness to mark where he thinks the house is where the victim was hit at the balcony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I've just placed a red dot where I believe that house is located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You earlier said "approximately there." I do not know where there's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately. You are correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- any more precise way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's just disappeared again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It just disappeared again. We are -- I think it would be wiser, Mr. Lukic, if we adjourn early today --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will lose only a couple of minutes and it will speed up if we have system working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it would be better to -- because now going back to the previous subject doesn't make much sense. Everyone gets confused. First, Mr. Hogan, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 but then in Courtroom I again. And I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, apart from technical problem, how much time you think you would still need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you telling me that you have problem with me because I want more time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I was talking about technical problems, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I understood, we have only one more witness coming this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is the Chamber in receipt of the e-mail and new schedule that I sent about an hour and a half ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am afraid that I have not seen that. But could I immediately look at it, if it is already sent to -- let me have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't think that we have received anything yet. Could you summarise the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The gist of it is, Your Honour, that based on what the Chamber has asked us to do with respect to Mr. Theunens, although last Friday I believed I could do that, and as much -- as hard as we tried over the weekend, it isn't possible to call him this week, so we're going to be rescheduling him to the second week in November. During that time we'll make the proposal that the Chamber has requested. We'll sit down and talk with the Defence about what is truly in contention in the report, and as Mr. Ivetic was requesting notice about the documents, we will be able at that stage to identify which documents we'll be using in the first part of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that means what exactly for this week's schedule? I remember having seeing an e-mail in which you said he was not available [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We tried with a couple of witnesses and came close with Mr. Higgs but he is not able to be here. There is a witness that is arriving I believe today, but he's represented, and we won't be able to speak to him until his lawyer appears. We will attempt to advance that witness to Thursday. But other than that, there is no other witnesses that we can call this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that means if we finish Mr. Hogan tomorrow - I'm looking at you, Mr. Lukic - tomorrow -- we would have no witness for Wednesday but perhaps for Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That perhaps makes life a bit more easy for you, Mr. Lukic, and you know what the Chamber always seeks to achieve. Then we adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 1st of October, in Courtroom I, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 1st day of October, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.14 p.m.,
